items.title: Software Update Caused US Flight Ground Stop
points: FAA issued a nationwide halt Friday after a communications failure hit air traffic control centers; order lifted at 8:15 pm ET after more than 4 hours, with delays expected for several days
A software update on L3Harris' private network rebooted and crashed, likely causing the outage; neither Microsoft's recent week-long outage nor FAA's new AI systems were involved
No evidence hackers were behind the disruption, distinguishing this from a cybersecurity incident

items.title: Starship Reaches Orbit Despite Booster Failure
points: SpaceX's 15th Starship test flight reached orbit even though the Super Heavy booster failed during return and exploded about 27 minutes after liftoff from Texas
Starship fired its engines in orbit with mission controllers' permission and deployed 26 Starlink satellites, meeting the main test flight goals
The Super Heavy booster was meant to return to the launch tower for catching by mechanical arms called 'Chopsticks,' but an automatic abort sent it into the Gulf of Mexico instead

items.title: Tesla Cybercab Pricing and Restrictions
points: The two-seat, $29,990 Cybercab sold to Austin-area customers has no steering wheel; touchscreen controls permit only 2 mph creep without a $299/month Autonomy Subscription (a recurring fee required to enable self-driving features)

Owners are limited to personal use inside Tesla's Robotaxi geofences (geographically defined zones where the service operates); commercial ride-hailing, delivery, or renting requires separate written permission from Tesla
Reselling or transferring a Cybercab without Tesla's approval triggers a minimum $50,000 penalty; Elon Musk said on X that the subscription price should match Full Self-Driving's ~$115 monthly cost

items.title: Google Smart Glasses Privacy: Auto-Blur Faces for AI Analysis
points: Google's upcoming Android XR smart glasses automatically blur or redact people's faces in photos and video before sending images to servers for analysis by Gemini, Google's AI assistant (e.g., translating menus, identifying objects)
Blurring applies whenever the wearer asks Gemini something, and also hides the wearer's own face when pointing the glasses at a mirror

Google says images won't be saved in Gemini history, used for AI training, or used for ads; Play Store apps are barred from real-time facial recognition, live-streaming, or disabling the recording light

items.title: OpenAI Disbands Robotics Team Again
points: OpenAI dissolved its robotics team again, folding researchers into its main research group
The move follows OpenAI's determination that general AI models like a hypothetical 'GPT-6 Astra' can control robots directly without needing a specialized robotics team
